To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
obese youth, compared to their normal-weight counterparts, reported poorer Qol, more internalizing and externalising problems, and higher BID.
obesity is associated with lower quality of life, higher levels of internalizing and external problems and higher body image dissatisfaction.
obesity is associated with decreased QOL and increased rates of internalizing/externalization problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of BID in the psychosocial adjustment of children and adolescents with obesity, and its role as a potential mediator between obesity and decreased QO.
the role of body dissatisfaction in the association between pediatric obesity and psychosocial functioning, and its moderating effect of age and gender.
the importance of BID as a mediator between weight status and decreased QOL, and as a predictor for internalizing/externalization problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
obesity and BID are associated with poorer psychopathology and QOL, and that BID is an important mediator of these associations.
BID is a mediator in the relationship between weight and quality of life, but it is only for youth above the age of 12.
BID seems to be an important mediator between weight status and decreased QOL for older youth, and a direct and independent predictor of internalizing/externalization problems for all youth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BID is a key mediator of the association between weight status and decreased QOL in adolescents, but it is not a mediator in younger children.
the associations of obesity with psychosocial outcomes are not uniform and depend on the age and gender of youth.
obesity is a serious health problem that has negative consequences on children’s and adolescents’ psychosocial functioning and that BID plays a significant role in these associations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the psychosocial functioning of obese youth can be improved by addressing BID.
BID is not only an important outcome of obesity in youth, but it also mediates some associations between weight status (obesity) and psychosocial outcomes (QOL).
BID is a significant mediator in the relationship between weight and QOL among older youth.
